From there, two activities take place in parallel: any errors are reported to the relevant team member, and a three-way match is double-checked. Once both are completed, the flow continues and fans out into three concurrent strands: a voucher is created for the documents, the items are stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account. Within the voucher strand, the work divides again so that the dates are checked to avoid penalty charges while, at the same time, the payment is scheduled. When both of these are finished, they converge and then rejoin with the other two strands (the storage and the accounts payable entry). After all three strands have completed, the process concludes.

If the assessment shows that no optimization is required, the process ends immediately. If optimization is required, once both identification and assessment are complete, the process continues to define the process completion time, then to write potential process improvements, and then to obtain approval for those improvements. Next, two activities are carried out in parallel: the updated process is used while success criteria for the improvements are defined. When both are complete, the process advances to perform two further branches in parallel: communicating the process changes and scheduling the next process review and optimization. On the communication branch, the changes are then implemented. After both the implementation of communicated changes and the scheduling are finished, the process concludes.

0.text: The process starts with checking the ticket type. From there, the work proceeds in parallel to perform multiple determinations: one assesses whether it is a Marketing/PR Question, another examines whether it is a Technical Issue, and a third checks whether it is a Simple Question. If it is examined as a Technical Issue, this is followed by determining whether it is a Feature Request, after which the issue is replicated. Once the Marketing/PR assessment, the Simple Question assessment, and the replication that follows the Technical Issue and Feature Request determinations have all been completed, the paths come together and the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and the ticket is first checked. Based on this check, one or more applicable ticket types can be selected: Marketing/PR Question, Technical Issue, and/or Simple Question. For a Marketing/PR Question, the determination is made and that path is complete. For a Simple Question, the determination is made and that path is complete. If a Technical Issue applies, it leads to determining whether it is a Feature Request, and then the issue is replicated. Once all of the selected paths (whichever were chosen) have been completed, the results are brought together and the process ends.

If the technical path is selected, it continues with Determine ticket type: Feature Request and then Replicate issue. Once all of the selected paths (any combination of the Marketing/PR, Simple Question, and the full technical path through feature request and replication) have been completed, the process proceeds to end.

0.text: The process starts and the order details are recorded. The work then splits so that two activities proceed in parallel: the products are checked to be in stock while, at the same time, the products taken from storage are recorded. Once the stock check is done, the ordered products are requested from inventory; in parallel, after recording the products taken, quality checks are performed. When both of these strands are finished, the flow continues to a point where one or both of the following may be carried out: the items are packaged securely and approval is obtained. After whichever of these selected activities have been completed, the flow proceeds to a set of simultaneous post-approval tasks in which the packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the shipping label is attached to the packaging. After the label has been attached, the invoice is printed, then the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and the order details are recorded. Work then splits into two parallel strands: one checks that the products are in stock and, based on that, requests the ordered products from inventory; the other records the products taken from storage and then performs quality checks. Once both strands are completed, the flow continues and optionally proceeds with one or both of the following: packaging the items securely, and seeking approval. If approval is sought, this triggers three activities to be carried out in parallel: printing the packing slip, measuring the products, and attaching the shipping label to the packaging. When these three are finished, the invoice is printed. The process then synchronizes, waiting for the completion of the packaging path if it was taken and for the invoicing path if approval was taken. After this synchronization, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

2.text: The process starts with recording the order details. Immediately afterward, the work splits into two parallel strands: one checks whether the products are in stock and then requests the ordered products from inventory, while the other records the products taken from storage and then performs quality checks. These strands finish together before a selection is made where one or both of the following paths may proceed: packaging the items securely and/or obtaining an approval. If packaging is selected, it proceeds on its own toward the later merge. If approval is selected, it triggers a further fan-out of post-approval work that runs in parallel: printing the packing slip, measuring the products, and attaching the shipping label to the packaging; once the label is attached, the invoice is printed, and then the packing slip, measurement, and invoice results are brought back together. At that point, whatever came from the earlier packaging step and the completed post-approval work converge, after which the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends. 0.text: The process starts and first the basic information is confirmed. Then the work splits: one track assesses the performance of the process while another identifies the process components and confirms whether the process requires optimization. Once both tracks are complete, the results are synchronized and the work splits again. One branch assesses if any steps are confusing. In parallel, another branch notes which steps can be automated, and from that branch the work further divides to define how long it takes to complete the process and to examine potentially wasteful steps. Once all three reviews are finished, the work converges and continues with checking the quarterly projections, then projecting the market share, and finally checking past lawsuits. The process completes when these checks are done.

0.text: The process starts when the borrower provides a bank statement to the lender and then completes the loan application. At that point, three activities proceed simultaneously: the lender gives written notice to the applicant, sends the application back to the applicant, and checks the application for completeness. Once all three of these have finished, the lender begins the underwriting process. This triggers three underwriting actions to run at the same time: the loan amount is reduced, the loan application is approved, and the interest rate is changed. Only after all three underwriting actions are completed does the borrower receive the loan funds, after which the process ends.

Once both are completed, ways of achieving the goals are determined. The other path assigns management responsibilities, which immediately triggers two parallel follow-up activities: obtaining approval from top management and incorporating the results into the master budget; these two converge before moving toward closing. If both the request to top management and the responsibilities path were initiated, the process waits for completion of both before closing; otherwise it closes after the single active path completes. The process then ends.

0.text: The process starts and the team records the customer’s basic details. Immediately after, three activities proceed in parallel: they analyze how the customer uses the product, determine ways to increase its value, and identify key points of value. Once the usage analysis is complete, they quantify the impact of cancellation, and when that, together with the work on determining ways to increase value and identifying key value points, is finished, the pre-call stage is complete. Next, two activities are carried out in parallel: they confirm the call date and time and give the customer a call. From the confirmation step, they proceed to optionally capture whether the customer responded and whether the customer is willing to talk; if they record the response status, they then send an email accordingly. When the email (if any) and the willingness-to-talk outcome have both been recorded, and the call itself is also finished, the team moves on to understand the reasons for leaving by performing, as applicable, both summarizing why the customer wants to leave and asking open-ended questions; when these are completed, they proceed to propose value in parallel by describing ideas to increase value, presenting a special offer, and informing the customer of key metrics that demonstrate value. After all proposals are done, they begin the wrap-up, which may include thanking the customer for their time and feedback and recording the customer’s decision; once these wrap-up items are completed, they ask if the customer has any other concerns, note down important learnings from the conversation, and then the process ends.

9.text: The process starts, after which the ticket is examined and its type is determined as “Sales Question.” The issue is then replicated initially, and the outcome is assessed to see whether everyone could replicate it. Based on this, the work may proceed along one or both of the following activities: prioritizing three to five goals and defining three to five goals. Once all selected goals-related activities are completed, the total annual budget is calculated. Next, income-related work may proceed along one or both of these activities: projecting total annual income and listing all sources of income. When the selected income-related activities are finished, the budget is finalized. After finalization, the process may continue with assigning management responsibilities and/or obtaining approval from top management. If management responsibilities are assigned, further work may proceed with requesting approval from top management and/or incorporating the result into the master budget. Once the selected post-assignment activities are completed, they rejoin the main path and synchronize with the path that obtained approval from top management. The process then concludes.

Immediately after, two activities proceed at the same time: confirming whether the process requires optimization and identifying the process’s components. Once both are completed, the analysis paths are selected, allowing one or more of the following to be performed: defining how long the process takes, noting which steps can be automated, and considering where bottlenecks occur. If the duration is defined, this leads to two concurrent activities—assessing whether any steps are confusing and looking to see if the process can be simplified—which then come back together. In parallel with or instead of that, any notes on automation are passed forward as-is, and any consideration of bottlenecks continues with examining potentially wasteful steps before joining the others. When these selected analyses have all converged, the potential process improvements are written up and then sent for approval. After approval, two follow-ups happen at the same time: determining which improvements should go forward and adding feedback on the updated process. These are brought together and used to prepare implementation with two concurrent activities: determining how the process will be monitored and communicating the process changes. 0.text: The workflow starts when the requester creates a purchase requisition. Depending on what is required, manager approval and finance approval may be sought; once all approvals that are needed have been obtained, procurement proceeds to prepare the order. Preparation happens in parallel: procurement informs the supplier that the order is ready for approval while also creating the purchase order. When both preparation activities are completed, the supplier is asked to approve the order. After the supplier’s approval, one or more follow‑up actions take place: the supplier may confirm the delivery date, after which procurement files the purchase order, and procurement may also record the purchase order. The process finishes once all of the selected follow‑up actions have been completed, after which it ends.

0.text: The process starts, after which the applicant fills the employment information form and then completes the loan application. At this point, one or more post-application actions are carried out: the applicant may be given written notice, and the application may be checked for completeness. If written notice is given, the application is sent back to the applicant; these selected actions then come together before proceeding. Next, the underwriting process begins. Its outcomes can include one or more of the following: changing the interest rate, approving the loan application, and reducing the loan amount. Once all selected outcomes have been completed, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and the applicant fills in the employment information form, then completes the loan application. After that, one or more post-application actions are carried out in parallel: the lender may give written notice to the applicant and, separately, check for completeness. If written notice is given, the application is then sent back to the applicant before converging with the other selected actions. Once all chosen post-application actions are finished, the process continues to begin the underwriting process. From there, one or more underwriting outcomes may occur: the interest rate may be changed, the loan application may be approved, and/or the loan amount may be reduced. After all selected outcomes are completed, the process proceeds to the applicant receiving the loan funds, and then ends.

0.text: The process starts and the agent first records basic details, then identifies key points of value. At this point, one or more outreach paths are selected: sending an email, confirming a call date and time, and/or recording whether the customer is willing to talk. If the email path is selected, after sending the email the work splits into two activities carried out in parallel: recording whether the customer responded and giving them a call; these two are completed and then brought back together before rejoining the other selected outreach paths. The outcomes of all selected outreach paths are then merged, after which the work immediately splits into three activities that proceed in parallel: asking open-ended questions, summarizing why the customer wants to leave, and identifying the root causes of the problem; these three are all completed and brought back together. Next, the work splits again into two activities performed in parallel: informing the customer of key metrics that demonstrate value and presenting a special offer; when both are done they rejoin. The process then splits once more into two parallel activities: thanking the customer for their time and feedback and recording the customer’s decision; these are completed and brought back together. Finally, the agent asks if the customer has any other concerns, sends the learnings to the appropriate managers, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and first a summary of the content is prepared. Based on this, a selection is made to share on social media and/or to comment on related blog posts; either one or both can be carried out. If sharing on social media is performed, it proceeds directly to the final consolidation. If commenting on related blog posts is performed, the flow continues with a further selection to post on related forums and/or to deep-link from older posts. Deep-linking from older posts, when chosen, moves to the consolidation for that stage, while posting on forums and groups leads on to another selection where outreach and/or repurposing may be performed. Outreach, if performed, heads to consolidation for that stage, while repurposing continues with yet another choice to post on Q&A sites and/or to pay for promotion. Posting on Q&A sites and paying for promotion, whichever are chosen, both feed into a consolidation that then returns to the outreach/repurposing consolidation, which in turn returns to the forum/deep-linking consolidation, and finally to the initial consolidation together with any earlier social sharing. Once all selected activities across these branches have completed and merged, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts with the applicant, who fills out the employment information form. Immediately afterward, two paths proceed in parallel: the applicant completes the loan application while, in the credit department, the application is received; the latter occurs upon submission of the application, which is communicated from the applicant to Credit Operations. Once both completion and receipt are done, the credit department proceeds to notify the applicant: depending on the case, the application may be sent back to the applicant, a written notice may be issued, or both actions may be carried out; these notifications conclude before the process continues. Next, the credit department runs two activities concurrently: it begins the underwriting process and also checks the credit score and risk score. When both are finished, the process advances to decision steps that also proceed in parallel: the interest rate is changed, leading to a reduction of the loan amount, while separately the loan application is approved. After the loan reduction and the approval both complete, the process moves to funding, and the applicant receives the loan funds. The process ends thereafter.

0.text: In Procurement, the requester begins by creating a purchase requisition and then waits for finance to approve it. As soon as the requisition is created, it is sent to the Finance Team; there, the finance approver runs their own approval, after which they finish and notify the requester, allowing the requester to proceed past the wait. The requester then informs the supplier that the order is ready for approval and subsequently waits for the supplier’s decision. Upon receiving that notification, the supplier runs their own order approval and, once finished, sends the outcome back to the requester, which releases the requester from the wait. The requester then records the purchase order and completes their process.

0.text: The process starts with setting a target date for approval. Next, pre-checks are carried out, consisting of one or both of the following: evaluating significant variances and reviewing the most recent budget; after whichever of these were selected are completed, preparation for goals begins by running two activities at the same time: defining three to five goals and determining ways of achieving the goals. Once the ways of achieving the goals are determined, the goals are prioritized; when both the goal definition and the prioritization are finished, budget calculations proceed, performing one or both of the following as needed: calculating the total annual budget and estimating the average monthly cost. After the selected budget calculations are completed, the total annual income is projected. Based on that, one or both of the following are then performed: finalizing the budget and recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet; once the chosen post-income tasks are done, approval-related work runs in parallel by both obtaining approval from top management and requesting approval from top management. After approval has been obtained, two follow-up actions proceed concurrently: assigning management responsibilities and incorporating into the master budget. When those two actions are finished, and the request for approval activity is also completed, the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and a target date for approval is set. Next, one or both preparatory analyses are carried out: significant variances are evaluated and the most recent budget is reviewed; once the selected analyses are completed, work proceeds to prepare goals. At this point two activities run at the same time: three to five goals are defined, and ways of achieving those goals are determined, after which the goals are prioritized. When the goals have been both defined and prioritized, budget calculations begin, where one or both of the following are performed: the total annual budget is calculated and the average monthly cost is estimated. These results are then brought together to project the total annual income. Based on that, one or both subsequent tasks are executed: the budget is finalized and the financial data are recorded in a budget spreadsheet, before converging again. Approvals are then handled in parallel: approval is obtained from top management while, in parallel, a request for approval is sent to top management. After approval has been obtained, two follow-up actions proceed simultaneously: management responsibilities are assigned and the budget is incorporated into the master budget. Finally, the branch that sent the approval request and the two post-approval actions synchronize, and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts, and the ticket is checked to identify its type. Based on this, all applicable main types are selected: this can include “Marketing/PR Question” and/or “Technical Issue.” For Marketing/PR, applicable subtypes are then chosen: “Feature Request” and/or “I’m not sure question.” If “Feature Request” applies, it is handled and waits to be combined with any other selected Marketing/PR subtypes. If “I’m not sure question” applies, it is split into two activities that proceed at the same time: “App Question” and “Mixed-type question.” Once both are completed, they are combined and then merged with any “Feature Request” outcome to complete the Marketing/PR branch. In parallel at the main level, if “Technical Issue” was selected, it proceeds directly to the point where all chosen main types are brought back together. After all selected main and subtype determinations are completed and combined, three resolution activities are executed simultaneously: “Replicate the issue,” “Respond to ticket question,” and “Test technical issues.” When all three are finished, the process ends.

1.text: The process starts and the ticket type is checked. Based on this, one or more initial paths may be taken: determining whether it is a Marketing/PR question and/or identifying it as a technical issue can proceed in parallel. If the Marketing/PR path is taken, one or more subtypes are selected: determining it as a feature request may be carried out, and/or identifying it as an “I’m not sure” question. If “I’m not sure” is selected, this is split into two simultaneous activities—determining it as an app question and determining it as a mixed-type question—which must both finish before the Marketing/PR path continues. The Marketing/PR outcomes (feature request and/or the concluded “I’m not sure” analysis) are then merged and brought together with the technical issue determination, after which the resolution work starts in parallel: replicating the issue, responding to the ticket question, and testing technical issues are executed simultaneously. 0.text: The process starts by confirming that payment has been received. Next, a set of pre-check activities is selected and carried out: performing quality checks, checking whether the products are in stock, and recording products taken from storage. Any combination of these may be executed; if the stock check is performed, it is followed by requesting the ordered products from inventory before the pre-checks conclude. Once all selected pre-checks are finished, a packing slip is printed. Packaging and preparation then proceed at the same time: other orders are examined for potential delivery overlaps, which leads to arranging the delivery, while in parallel the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle. After both arranging the delivery and loading are completed, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends. There are no external communications depicted.

After the packing slip is printed, two pre-shipment activities run at the same time: examining other orders for possible delivery overlaps and loading the items into the delivery vehicle. Once the examination of overlaps is finished, the delivery is arranged; when both the loading and the arranging of delivery are completed, they rejoin. This rejoin feeds into the same waiting point that also collects the completion of the other selected preparatory activities (quality checks and recording products taken from storage), and that point waits only for those activities that were actually selected earlier. 0.text: The process begins with the borrower providing a bank statement to the lender and then completing the loan application. Once submitted, the lender proceeds on two tracks at the same time: they issue a written notice to the applicant and they send the application back to the applicant. From sending it back, the lender determines whether the application is complete; if it is complete, this track proceeds to rejoin the other, and if it is incomplete, the lender checks completeness and then reassesses until it is deemed complete, at which point it also rejoins. After both the written notice and the completeness track have finished, the lender carries out two activities in parallel: they begin the underwriting process and they check the credit and risk scores. When both are finished, the lender may adjust terms on two fronts concurrently by reducing the loan amount and changing the interest rate, and continues only after both adjustments are completed. Finally, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process concludes.

Once both are completed, the next step is to prioritize three to five goals. Based on those priorities, one or both of the following are performed as needed: the average monthly cost is estimated and the total annual budget is calculated. When these are finished, all sources of income are listed. Next, the work splits so that the budget is finalized and the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet at the same time. After both are done, the flow proceeds to a further split where management responsibilities are assigned in parallel with requesting approval from top management. When these parallel activities are completed, the process concludes.

0.text: The process starts and proceeds to make an introduction, after which the work branches so that recording the basic idea and identifying the approval status can run in parallel. From the approval status, one or both of the following may be carried out: working out the value and getting approval; whichever of these are chosen later come back together and then wait until the recorded basic idea is also available. Once both the basic idea and the chosen approval-related activities are complete, the work splits into three concurrent strands: laying out the timeline, drawing up the project plan, and setting the budget. After the project plan is drawn up, the available resources are stated, and then the process waits until the timeline, the budget, and the available resources are all ready. Next comes the kickoff meeting, followed by recording the KPIs, after which the flow splits so that evaluating the project outcomes and ensuring the project is completed can proceed in parallel. When the evaluation is finished, contractors are terminated, and this outcome is synchronized with the completion activity; once both the termination and the completion have been reached, the process ends.

Next, one or more team-related reviews are carried out: the team’s chemistry may be reviewed, the individual’s ability as a team leader may be reviewed, and the number of employees may be reviewed; once all selected reviews are done, the results are brought together. The process then moves to financial checks, where one or more activities are performed: cash flow may be checked, income statements may be checked, and the exit strategy may be checked. 0.text: The process starts by unmuting all gradebook columns. It then splits so that preparing grades for SSO can proceed in parallel with importing the gradebook. From the import, work branches again into three concurrent activities: selecting the exam assignment, calculating the grades, and applying special grades to individuals. After calculation, the score criteria are applied, and then these three import-related activities converge. Their result is combined with the completed preparation for SSO, ensuring all preceding work is finished before continuing. Next, the grades summary is reviewed, the final grades are exported, and the results are submitted to SSO, which completes the process.

1.text: The process starts and the gradebook columns are first unmuted. Work then splits into two concurrent pre-tasks: in one branch, grades are prepared for submission to the student system; in the other, the gradebook is imported. The import branch immediately divides into three parallel steps: the exam assignment is selected; the grades are calculated and then the score criteria are applied in sequence; and any special grades are applied to individual students. Once the exam assignment is selected, the score criteria have been applied after calculation, and all special grades have been set, these three import steps converge. That completed import branch then meets the other pre-task where grades were prepared, and only when both branches are finished does the process continue. The results are reviewed in a summary, the final grades are exported, and the results are submitted to the student system, after which the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and begins with making an introduction. Immediately afterward, two activities run in parallel: creating accounts and obtaining the initial approval; once both are finished, the flow proceeds to launch three parallel tracks: touring the office, holding a welcoming ceremony, and assigning a mentor. When the mentor has been assigned, three further activities run in parallel within that branch—explaining expectations, inducting the new hire into the company culture, and assigning training material—and all three must finish. In the meantime, the office tour and the welcoming ceremony proceed independently; the process waits until the tour, the ceremony, and the three activities following mentor assignment have all completed. It then continues to carry out two activities in parallel—obtaining the final approval and checking paperwork—and only after both are completed does it move on to optionally perform one or more wrap-up actions: explaining long-term goals, reviewing onboarding over the next 60 days, and encouraging social interaction with the team. After all of the selected wrap-up actions have concluded, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and first the basic information is confirmed. Work then proceeds in parallel to confirm whether the process requires optimization and to identify its components; once both are done, the results are brought together and a choice is made about which analyses to perform. Depending on what is selected, the team may assess whether any steps are confusing and/or consider where bottlenecks occur. If confusing steps are assessed, this branches into two concurrent activities: defining the overall completion time for the process and looking for ways to simplify it; these two strands are then brought back together. In the bottleneck track, after considering where bottlenecks occur, potentially wasteful steps are examined. All analysis outcomes are then merged, after which potential process improvements are written and sent for approval. With approval in hand, one or both of the following may occur: defining what would make the improvements successful and choosing who will test the updated process. If testers are chosen, the next part may include updating process documents and/or starting to use the updated process; these come back together and, together with the defined success criteria (if produced), converge before the final execution step. The process then splits into two parallel activities to communicate the process changes and to implement the process changes; when both are completed, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts with creating a purchase requisition. This triggers two approvals that proceed in parallel: one from the finance team and one from the manager. Once both approvals are completed, the work continues by branching into two preparatory activities in parallel: informing the supplier that the order is ready for approval and creating the purchase order. When both of these are done, the supplier is asked to approve. After the supplier’s approval, the flow may proceed with any combination of the following actions: sending the details to the department, confirming the delivery date, and recording the purchase order. If the delivery date is confirmed, the purchase order is then filed; the other two actions proceed directly. The process then waits until all of the post-supplier actions that were started have completed, and finally ends.
